rationale: This is a pure re-weighting of three legs already tested in FragilityIndexFourLeg, EarningsDownsideAsymmetryWithFundingGap and DownsideAsymmetryWithCashOnly, so it is a cosmetic weighting variant rather than a new mechanism, and the claim that it will "convert" the leader's weak FMB slope by adding a 25%-weight leg is not credible since the vol leg's own slope (-2.5) was obtained in a different pairing.

Same objection as the previous proposal — it substitutes one already-tested archive leg (trough coverage) for another (revenue vol) inside an identical nested SUMRANK, which is an attribution exercise on weights rather than a substantively different signal, and the two candidates are near-duplicates of each other.

Applying the downside-tail transform to the coverage ratio instead of the margin is a real mechanism change and the expression matches the hypothesis, though it overlaps meaningfully with CoverageDrawdownUnderLeverage (peak-relative coverage decline) and risks inheriting that signal's mediocre alpha since (pi+dp)/lt asymmetry is largely a scaled version of pi-margin asymmetry when lt is stable.

Retained-earnings flow is a genuinely unused channel in this archive and the construction is internally consistent, but the reviewer should note that DELTA(re) is close to net income less dividends and RE/assets is a classic Altman Z-score input, so partial rediscovery of the profitability/distress-score literature is a live risk.

The test is confounded — it simultaneously changes the liquidity denominator (act to lct) and adds a three-year TS_MIN, so a change in alpha versus DownsideAsymmetryWithCashOnly cannot be attributed to the tail transformation, and che/lct in various forms has already appeared in five archive signals.

A clean, well-motivated ablation that completes the (dlc−che)/act decomposition the archive left half-finished and whose sign convention is internally consistent; it is diagnostic rather than novel, so its value depends entirely on the follow-up being drawn from the outcome rather than on the signal itself.
